current_news.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
current_news.facts: Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface. OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters. The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

window_news.title: Cheniere Signs Long-Term Sale and Purchase Agreements to Supply QatarEnergy with LNG through 2054
window_news.facts: (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries,… (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries, Sabine Pass Liquefaction, LLC (“SPL”) and Corpus Christi Liquefaction, LLC (“CCL”), have each entered into long-term liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) sale and purchase agreements (“SPA”) with QatarEnergy to supply a total of 4 million tonnes per annum (“mtpa”) of LNG through 2054. (NYSE: CQP), we are developing an expansion of the existing Sabine Pass Liquefaction Project (“SPL Project”) with an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG (the “SPL Expansion Project”), inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities, which would grow the total production capacity of the SPL Project to over 50 mtpa of LNG. We expect to execute the SPL Expansion Project in a phased approach. The first phase is expected to include a single train, Train 7, and a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, along with supporting infrastructure and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass LNG terminal, and has an expected total production capacity of over 6 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. (“Bechtel”) for the first phase of the SPL Expansion Project was signed, and Bechtel was released to commence early engineering and procurement under a limited notice to proceed (LNTP).

window_news.title: Cook Inlet LNG steps up Alaska energy push with TDI-Brooks survey
window_news.facts: TDI-Brooks has completed a geotechnical mission, bolstering Cook Inlet LNG’s efforts to shore up Southcentral Alaska’s energy supplies. U.S.-headquartered geotechnical and offshore survey research and service company TDI-Brooks has wrapped up a critical geotechnical campaign for Cook Inlet LNG, a strategic initiative designed to secure natural gas supplies for Southcentral Alaska, delivering vital subsurface data to support the project's anchor selection and helping bring the developer’s floating import terminal aspirations closer to reality. TDI-Brooks has concluded a geotechnical project for the Cook Inlet LNG project (CI LNG) in Cook Inlet, Alaska, providing its Neptune N5K cone penetration testing (CPT) system for an anchor site characterization study. The work supported the project developer by collecting subsurface soil data to inform anchor selection. player, the study covered different locations within the project site with a scope of 16 CPTs in water depths ranging from 10 to 25 meters. The Cook Inlet LNG project is an energy security initiative designed to address declining natural gas reserves in the Cook Inlet basin of Southcentral Alaska to stave off a potential energy shortfall for heating and electricity by serving as a near-term bridge solution to import gas.

current_news.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
current_news.facts: Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface. OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters. The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

window_news.title: Cheniere Signs Long-Term Sale and Purchase Agreements to Supply QatarEnergy with LNG through 2054
window_news.facts: (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries,… (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries, Sabine Pass Liquefaction, LLC (“SPL”) and Corpus Christi Liquefaction, LLC (“CCL”), have each entered into long-term liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) sale and purchase agreements (“SPA”) with QatarEnergy to supply a total of 4 million tonnes per annum (“mtpa”) of LNG through 2054. (NYSE: CQP), we are developing an expansion of the existing Sabine Pass Liquefaction Project (“SPL Project”) with an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG (the “SPL Expansion Project”), inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities, which would grow the total production capacity of the SPL Project to over 50 mtpa of LNG. We expect to execute the SPL Expansion Project in a phased approach. The first phase is expected to include a single train, Train 7, and a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, along with supporting infrastructure and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass LNG terminal, and has an expected total production capacity of over 6 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. (“Bechtel”) for the first phase of the SPL Expansion Project was signed, and Bechtel was released to commence early engineering and procurement under a limited notice to proceed (LNTP).

window_news.title: Cook Inlet LNG steps up Alaska energy push with TDI-Brooks survey
window_news.facts: TDI-Brooks has completed a geotechnical mission, bolstering Cook Inlet LNG’s efforts to shore up Southcentral Alaska’s energy supplies. U.S.-headquartered geotechnical and offshore survey research and service company TDI-Brooks has wrapped up a critical geotechnical campaign for Cook Inlet LNG, a strategic initiative designed to secure natural gas supplies for Southcentral Alaska, delivering vital subsurface data to support the project's anchor selection and helping bring the developer’s floating import terminal aspirations closer to reality. TDI-Brooks has concluded a geotechnical project for the Cook Inlet LNG project (CI LNG) in Cook Inlet, Alaska, providing its Neptune N5K cone penetration testing (CPT) system for an anchor site characterization study. The work supported the project developer by collecting subsurface soil data to inform anchor selection. player, the study covered different locations within the project site with a scope of 16 CPTs in water depths ranging from 10 to 25 meters. The Cook Inlet LNG project is an energy security initiative designed to address declining natural gas reserves in the Cook Inlet basin of Southcentral Alaska to stave off a potential energy shortfall for heating and electricity by serving as a near-term bridge solution to import gas.
